speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for the past two months. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if this pain occurs with activity or if it is present even when you are resting?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) or Osgood-Schlatter Disease (given age 24, Osgood-Schlatter is less likely; could be early-onset Rheumatoid Arthritis or crystal arthropathy like CPPD). Given the severity (night pain) and lack of response to NSAIDs, I suspect an inflammatory or structural cause. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, Anti-CCP, and Uric Acid. REQUEST IMAGES: Left Knee X-ray (AP and Lateral).
